articles.title: 32º Grito dos Excluídos reúne manifestantes em defesa da moradia e do rio Tucunduba em Belém | G1
articles.standfirst: Mobilização ocorreu na Terra Firme e levou às ruas reivindicações por moradia, permanência no território, justiça ambiental e preservação do rio
articles.summary: Mobilização ocorreu na Terra Firme e levou às ruas reivindicações por moradia, permanência no território, justiça ambiental e preservação do rio
articles.body:
O 32º Grito dos Excluídos e das Excluídas foi realizado no sábado (5), no bairro da Terra Firme, em Belém, com uma caminhada em defesa da moradia, da permanência das famílias no território e da preservação do rio Tucunduba. A mobilização teve concentração no barracão do Boi Marronzinho e seguiu até a área onde está prevista a construção do Parque Linear do Tucunduba.

Com o tema permanente “Vida em Primeiro Lugar!” e o lema “Na defesa da Terra, da Paz e da Moradia, erguemos a voz: Mulheres Vivas e Soberania!”, o ato chamou atenção para problemas enfrentados por moradores da Terra Firme, como saneamento, insegurança fundiária, redução de áreas verdes e ameaças de remoção relacionadas às intervenções urbanas na região.

Entre as principais reivindicações apresentadas pelos movimentos está a defesa de uma urbanização que melhore as condições de moradia, saneamento e infraestrutura sem retirar moradores do território. As organizações também questionam aspectos do projeto do Parque Linear do Tucunduba, principalmente a retirada de vegetação prevista durante as obras.

A preservação do Tucunduba também esteve entre as pautas da mobilização. O rio continua sendo utilizado para o transporte de mercadorias por produtores das ilhas de Belém até a feira da Terra Firme. Os movimentos defendem que a recuperação ambiental e a melhoria do saneamento sejam feitas com a manutenção da navegabilidade.

A programação também reuniu intervenções políticas e culturais. Ao final da caminhada, estavam previstos o plantio de mudas e um foto varal do projeto Periferia Viva-Tucunduba Verde e Resiliente, iniciativa que reúne moradores, pesquisadores e poder público em ações relacionadas aos alagamentos, ao calor intenso e à falta de áreas verdes na bacia do Tucunduba.

articles.title: Universitário denuncia racismo após ofensas em foto vestindo jaleco | G1
articles.standfirst: João Lucas Brito, de 24 anos, compartilhou fotos do ensaio de formatura no Instagram e recebeu comentários de cunho racista e xenofóbico. Polícia Civil investiga o caso.
articles.summary: João Lucas Brito, de 24 anos, compartilhou fotos do ensaio de formatura no Instagram e recebeu comentários de cunho racista e xenofóbico de um médico. Polícia investiga o caso.
articles.body:
O estudante de medicina e doutorando João Lucas Brito, de 24 anos, denunciou ataques racistas e xenofóbicos numa postagem no Instagram . O caso aconteceu após o jovem compartilhar no seu perfil na rede sociais as fotos do ensaio de formatura ( veja vídeo acima ). Em uma delas, recebeu o comentário: "Saudades de quando favelado não entrava em medicina... Bons tempos".

A mensagem contra o recifense foi publicada por um médico de Brasília , que não conhece ou segue João Lucas nas redes sociais. O universitário registrou um boletim de ocorrência na sexta-feira (4), mas preferiu não revelar o nome do agressor. A Polícia Civil investiga o caso de "injúria praticada no ambiente virtual".

Em entrevista ao g1 , o jovem disse que, ao compartilhar as fotos, queria celebrar o fim da graduação. Ele não esperava a repercussão das imagens, que acabaram alcançando um público maior e diferente do esperado.

"Na cabeça dele, ele achava que aquilo ali [comentário] ia me atingir. Só que para mim não era um xingamento. Então na mente dele, me chamar de favelado era algo ruim. Só que para mim ser favelado é quem eu sou", disse João Lucas sobre o episódio.

A foto que recebeu o comentário é de João Lucas vestindo um jaleco de médico com seu nome bordado, um óculos de lentes espelhadas – modelo comum entre jovens de periferia. Ele também segura nas mãos o livro "Sobrevivendo no Inferno", do grupo de rap Racionais MC's.

João Lucas nasceu e cresceu no Recife , na Comunidade do Cardoso, que fica localizada no bairro da Madalena, na Zona Oeste da cidade. Ele conta que a escolha dos itens para as fotos partiu das suas vivências antes de ingressar na faculdade.

"Eu sempre escutava muitas músicas de Racionais. Pela comunidade Cardoso tocava Racionais, meus primos escutavam Racionais, minhas referências escutavam Racionais. Então, eu escutava Racionais, e eu usava muito a ideia do álbum de 'Sobrevivendo no inferno'", explicou o estudante.

Estudante de medicina denuncia racismo no Instagram em fotos usando jaleco — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Além de racistas, as mensagens do usuário do Instagram questionavam a credibilidade das instituições de ensino superior no Nordeste. Seguidores e amigos de João também responderam ao comentário, em defesa do jovem universitário.

Durante a discussão, o autor das injúrias se identificou como médico e divulgou o número do seu Conselho Regional de Medicina (CRM). Com os dados, João Lucas conseguiu registrar um boletim de ocorrência contra ele.

Com a repercussão do caso, o comentário com as ofensas foi removido do Instagram. Porém, João Lucas ainda tem prints das mensagens, que serão utilizados para auxiliar na investigação da polícia.

O estudante contou, ainda, que vai dar entrada em uma ação no Ministério Público de Pernambuco. "Para que essa situação não passe impune, porque a gente sofreu não só questões raciais, como questões de elitismo, questões também de xenofobia, questões também que envolvem as instituições públicas do nosso Estado, e isso é muito grave", pontuou o jovem.

Dois dias após o episódio, João também fez uma nova postagem nas redes sociais onde questiona: "Mas por que um médico favelado incomoda tanto?". Relembrando suas realizações ainda como estudante, o jovem escreveu que "nenhuma dessas conquistas é motivo pelo qual aquele comentário está errado. Eu não precisaria ter feito nada disso para merecer estar aqui".

O universitário será o primeiro médico da sua família. Atualmente, o jovem está no 11º período do curso de medicina em uma faculdade particular com bolsa integral pelo programa Programa Universidade para Todos (ProUni).

Aos 23 anos de idade, por causa do seu desempenho acadêmico, João Lucas foi aprovado no doutorado de Saúde Integral no Instituto de Medicina Integral Professor Fernando Figueira (Imip).

A oportunidade foi possível através do programa Programa MD-PhD, regulamentado pela Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior (Capes). Ele desenvolve uma pesquisa na pós-graduação ao mesmo tempo em que finaliza seu curso de medicina.

"É um estudo sobre as disparidades étnico-raciais dos nascidos vivos aqui no Brasil. Então, mesmo na minha pesquisa de doutorado, eu ainda continuo trazendo muito do que me representa. [...] Não tem como eu ignorar de onde eu venho. Então, uma forma que eu vejo de trazer retorno para minha comunidade é não sendo objeto de estudo, mas, sim, sendo produtor daquele conhecimento", disse ao g1 .

O cronograma do doutorado prevê, ainda, um intercâmbio no Canadá em 2027, para desenvolvimento da tese. A previsão é que a pesquisa seja finalizada em 2028.

articles.title: Jovem relata momentos de tensão ao ser arrastada por carro de aplicativo no interior de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Yasmin Marcondes do Carmo, de 15 anos, tem ferimentos no rosto, nos braços e nas pernas; motorista de 51 anos ainda não foi localizado.
articles.summary: Yasmin Marcondes do Carmo, de 15 anos, tem ferimentos no rosto, nos braços e nas pernas; motorista de 51 anos ainda não foi localizado.
articles.body:
A estudante Yasmin Marcondes do Carmo, de 15 anos, relatou neste domingo (6) os momentos de tensão que viveu ao ser arrastada por um carro de aplicativo na última sexta-feira (4) , em Tremembé , no interior de São Paulo. O motorista do veículo, de 51 anos, não foi localizado até a publicação desta reportagem.

Yasmin concedeu entrevista à TV Vanguarda acompanhada da tia, Selma Cristina Marcondes. Com ferimentos no rosto, nos braços e nas pernas, ela contou que solicitou a corrida pelo aplicativo para levar o irmão mais novo, de quatro anos, para a mãe. Disse que, como o irmão estava chorando quando entraram no carro, o motorista teria demonstrado impaciência. No meio do caminho, disse ter visto a mãe e solicitado ao motorista para parar o carro.

Yasmin Marcondes do Carmo foi arrastada por carro de aplicativo — Foto: Sávio Augusto/TV Vanguarda

Após descer para entregar o irmão e retornar ao carro para pagar a corrida, que teria custado R$ 12,60, ela diz que o motorista tomou da mão dela uma nota de R$ 100, não deu o troco e arrancou com o carro.

"Eu tive uma discussão com a minha mãe, desci do carro com meu irmão. Ele (motorista) foi um pouco à frente, fez a rotatória e voltou (para receber). Eu tinha esquecido dele. Ele veio xingando. Eu fui com uma nota de 100 para dar para ele. Ele puxou e, nisso que foi sair com o carro, me puxou junto. Eu fiquei grudada no carro. Eu grudei mais forte para não cair, mas eu vi que ele não iria parar o carro. Estava fazendo muito zigue-zague. Eu pulei e bati a cabeça, minha perna está toda roxa. Mesmo assim, ele não prestou socorro. Saiu correndo, quase atropelou a mulher que estava vindo. Eu tinha duas notas de 100, uma rasgou", contou Yasmin.

Ferimentos no braço de Yasmin Marcondes do Carmo — Foto: Sávio Augusto/TV Vanguarda

O caso ocorreu na Rua José Vicente de Barros, entre os bairros Vera Cruz e Parque Santo Antônio, em Tremembé. As imagens foram flagradas pelo COI de Tremembé. Nas imagens é possível ver o momento em que um carro branco acelera pela rua, sentido Tremembé, fazendo um zigue-zague. A vítima fica pendurada na porta do motorista (assista o vídeo acima) . As investigações continuam.

Após conseguir se desvencilhar do carro, Yasmin foi atendida e levada ao hospital pelo Samu.

"Na hora, eu só queria ir embora para minha casa. Não queria nem ir ao hospital. Eu estava bem consciente. Estava sentindo bastante dor na minha perna. O Samu chegou bem rápido. Não me recordo o que aconteceu. Só recordo quando já estava no chão. Não lembro muito. No dia, tive alta (do hospital). Não estava conseguindo mexer minha perna. Ontem consegui mexer. Hoje está melhor", afirmou.

articles.title: Mother Cow Stands Guard Over Her Calf in the Road Until Help Arrives
articles.summary: A calf lying motionless in a busy Nepal road drew no help from the cars and trucks steering around it, but its mother refused to leave its side until a stran...
articles.body:
A cow in Nepal was seen standing guard over her calf in the middle of a road as traffic passed by.

The video footage captured a passerby eventually carrying the calf to safety while the mother cow kept a watchful eye.

Asia is home to a significant portion of the world's cattle population, with nearly 460 million head in the region.

Cows can form strong bonds with their calves, and a mother may stay close or become protective when her calf appears vulnerable. That is what this brief clip seems to show: a cow stands over a calf lying in the road as traffic moves around them. A passerby eventually carries the calf to the roadside while the cow keeps watch. The video does not reveal why the calf was down, but the little family gets a safer place to regroup.

The short clip was filmed in the Debinagar area of Butwal, a city in Nepal's Rupandehi District in South Asia . A cow and calf are in the roadway, slowing traffic as vehicles work around them. ViralHog published the footage on June 5, 2023, under the title "Man Helps Mama Cow Move Calf Off Road." The page credits the video to Deepa.

The footage is shot from above, looking down on a road where a cow stands beside a calf lying on the pavement. The calf does not get up during this part of the clip, but the video alone cannot tell us whether it is injured, ill, exhausted, or simply resting.

The cow stays close to the calf and positions herself between it and some of the passing vehicles, behavior consistent with a mother keeping watch over her young. She also casts a shadow over part of the calf, although the clip does not establish whether she is deliberately shading it. Asia spans a wide range of climates , and without a date or weather reading for the recording, there is no sound basis for assigning a temperature to this scene.

A passerby approaches, lifts the calf, and carries it to the side of the road. The cow follows close behind and moves her head after the calf is set down. It is tempting to read the gesture as a thank-you—or a dismissal—but the video does not tell us what she meant. Either way, the calf is no longer lying in the traffic lane.

Domestic cattle belong to the family Bovidae. They are generally classified as Bos taurus , although zebu cattle may be classified as Bos indicus or as the subspecies Bos taurus indicus . The Food and Agriculture Organization reported nearly 1.6 billion cattle worldwide in 2023. People raise them across Africa , Asia, Europe, the Americas—including North America —and Oceania. Because cattle are domesticated livestock, their global numbers reflect human breeding and agriculture rather than the conservation status of a wild population.

Asia is home to hundreds of millions of cattle . FAO figures for 2023 put the region at 29% of the world's nearly 1.6 billion cattle—roughly 460 million head. The totals vary sharply by country. Taiwan has a relatively small herd, while India and China have Asia's largest cattle populations; together, they account for about 17% of the global total. In a separate measure, USDA estimates show India had about 59.5 million cows in milk in 2022 , more than any other country in its comparison. Domestic cattle are not a threatened wild species. Their numbers are managed by people, which also means their welfare is largely in human hands.

articles.title: Rajnath Singh to undertake 3-day visit to Sri Lanka from Tuesday, tour to strengthen bilateral, defence ties
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh will undertake an official visit to Sri Lanka from Tuesday for three days. His visit to the island nation wi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh will undertake an official visit to Sri Lanka from Tuesday for three days. His visit to the island nation will strengthen the traditionally strong and friendly bilateral relations in mutually beneficial areas, including a strong maritime and defence partnership.This will be the first visit of an Indian defence minister to the island nation in 38 years for defence-level talks. The last time an Indian defence minister visited Sri Lanka for defence talks was K C Pant, who travelled to the island nation in 1988 while serving in Rajiv Gandhi's Cabinet. Pranab Mukherjee did go to Sri Lanka as defence minister in Aug 2005 but he went only to attend the state funeral of Sri Lanka's foreign minister Lakshman Kadirgamar, who was assassinated.During his visit, Rajnath will hold consultations with the leadership of Sri Lanka on a range of issues and interact with the Indian diaspora in Colombo, a defence ministry’s release said on Sunday. He will lead a high-level delegation comprising senior officials from the defence ministry and the ministry of external affairs.India and Sri Lanka share deep civilisational ties and a multifaceted partnership, anchored by regional security, defence, economic and trade cooperation and strong people-to-people ties.The bilateral relationship received further impetus when India assisted Sri Lanka during the economic crisis and provided assistance, as one of the first responders, in the aftermath of Cyclone Ditwah in Sri Lanka in 2025. It underscored India’s continued commitment and emphasis on ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy and PM Narendra Modi’s vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

articles.title: Pat McAfee has put more than $6 million of his own money into GameDay prizes and charity; Home Depot matched his $500,000 LSU offer, giving one student two kicks at $1 million, but both missed
articles.summary: US News: An LSU undergraduate missed out on a life-changing $1 million (£760,000) prize on national television after missing two field goal attempts during ESP.
articles.body: An LSU undergraduate missed out on a life-changing $1 million (£760,000) prize on national television after missing two field goal attempts during ESPN's College GameDay broadcast in Baton Rouge. The high-stakes challenge saw sports analyst and former NFL punter Pat McAfee offer $500,000 from his own money. Show sponsor Home Depot then matched the amount, raising the total prize to $1 million. According to reports from EssentiallySports and Yahoo Sports, the contest took place during the 500th road broadcast of College GameDay, as the network began its 40th season outside Louisiana State University's campus quad. The huge prize was one of the biggest single-kick opportunities in the history of the weekly segment.Double trouble on the 33-yard markThe contestant, an LSU freshman named Bruce, was chosen through a random raffle from students who had arrived early inside the broadcast area. Under the contest rules, non-varsity students must make a standard 33-yard field goal. With $1 million at stake, Bruce stepped up for his first attempt, but the kick went wide. Following the segment's tradition of giving contestants a second chance, McAfee offered Bruce a mulligan for the full $1 million prize. However, the second kick also went wide, leaving the crowd disappointed and the prize unclaimed. After the second miss, McAfee posted a video of the kick on X with the caption: "NO GOOD AGAIN GOOD EFFORT BRUCE."Self-funded prizes and corporate matchingThe live kicking challenge has become one of College GameDay's best-known segments since McAfee introduced it during his second season as a permanent analyst. Since the feature began, McAfee has personally put more than $6 million of his own money into student prizes and direct charitable donations at university campuses across the US. "McAfee put up $500k for a successful kick. Home Depot said it would match whatever McAfee offered for the full season," EssentiallySports wrote in its report on the event. In previous contests, McAfee has donated money to charities or university hardship funds even when students missed their kicks. However, no additional charitable donation was announced after the Baton Rouge misses.A history of student windfallsAlthough the opening weekend ended without a winner, previous seasons have produced several student millionaires and large charitable donations. During the 2023 season, Washington student Greyson Wilhelm became the first contestant to make a winning kick. He won $30,000 on a second attempt. The prize amounts grew sharply in later seasons. In 2024, Georgia students Henry Silver and Belle Sessions shared a $400,000 prize after making a 33-yard kick. The successful attempt also triggered an additional $400,000 donation towards hurricane relief. Other major wins came at Vanderbilt, where student Tyler Hwang won $500,000 along with a $250,000 charitable donation. At Texas Tech, John Machtolff made a second-chance kick to win $250,000, with another $250,000 going to charity. With Home Depot promising to match McAfee's prize offers throughout the college football season, the weekly kicking challenge will continue giving students the chance to win seven-figure prizes at future College GameDay broadcast locations.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Twitch has temporarily suspended political streamer MikeFromPA after clips of his comments about fellow creator Hutch spread online. Many viewers believed MikeFromPA's words encouraged violence against Hutch, leading to major backlash. The exact reason for the suspension has not been publicly confirmed by Twitch. Hutch also said he contacted Twitch about the situation and reported the matter to the FBI. However, no agency has confirmed an investigation, and MikeFromPA's Twitch channel appeared to return shortly after the suspension.Twitch suspends MikeFromPA after Hutch comments spark backlashMikeFromPA, who is behind the Central_Committee streaming brand, is known for his left-wing political streams. Recently, clips of him talking about Hutch began spreading online.Critics said his comments sounded like he was encouraging someone to hurt or kill Hutch. The clips quickly caused anger across social media, with many viewers asking Twitch to take action.Hutch, who has been creating gaming and political content for many years, reportedly contacted Twitch directly about the situation. He also said he contacted the FBI.However, it is important to understand that making a report does not mean an investigation has started. No agency has publicly confirmed receiving the report or opening a case.Twitch later temporarily suspended MikeFromPA's account. But the platform did not publicly explain exactly why it took action. Twitch also did not say which rule was broken or how long the suspension would last.Why was MikeFromPA back on Twitch so quickly after suspension?The short suspension became another major part of the controversy. The action reportedly happened around the US Labor Day weekend, when MikeFromPA was not expected to stream anyway.Online reports gave different estimates for the suspension, ranging from one day to several days. Twitch itself did not confirm the length of the punishment. Soon after, MikeFromPA's channel appeared to be back online.This upset many viewers. Some argued that a short suspension was not enough if Twitch believed the comments broke its rules. Others pointed out that Twitch's Community Guidelines do not allow threats of violence or content that encourages people to commit violent acts.Twitch can give different punishments depending on the situation. These can range from warnings and temporary suspensions to indefinite bans. However, because Twitch has not explained its decision in this case, it remains unclear exactly what the company concluded about MikeFromPA's comments.MikeFromPA has also not shared the suspension email or given a detailed public explanation about his comments. For now, the brief Twitch suspension has left viewers with more questions than answers, while the backlash over his comments about Hutch continues online.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Corps Commanders of the Army and Chinese PLA Commanding formations in the eastern part of Arunachal Pradesh Sunday geared up for talks to sort out ongoing tensions along the state's stretch of the 1,126-km Line of Actual Control. The meeting is the first Corps Commander-level military talks in the eastern sector at the Vacha-Damai border meeting point.The latest talks are significant as India and China have so far held Corps Commander-level meetings primarily at the Chusul-Moldo border meeting point in the Ladakh sector. The latest engagement marks a new start from both sides to address issues in the eastern sector. A source told TOI, "The Indian side will be represented by Lieutenant General Girish Kalia, Commander of the Indian Army's 3 Corps, also known as Spear Corps."The 3 Corps is headquartered at Rangapahar in Nagaland and is responsible for operational areas along the LAC in Arunachal. The Army has two Corps formations looking after the LAC in the state, including Tezpur-based 4 Corps and Rangapahar-based 3 Corps.India and China have different perceptions of the LAC, resulting, at times, in face-offs. The latest engagement is expected to provide them with an opportunity to address such issues directly through military channels.The talks follow a meeting in Beijing in Aug between national security adviser Ajit Doval and China's foreign minister, Wang Yi. articles.title: AfD's Siegmund raises prospect of new election in Saxony-Anhalt
articles.summary: Ulrich Siegmund, lead candidate for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), has raised the prospect of new elections in Saxony-Anhalt if no majority can...
articles.body:
Ulrich Siegmund, lead candidate for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), has raised the prospect of new elections in Saxony-Anhalt if no majority can be formed in the state parliament following Sunday's vote.

The latest projections show Siegmund's AfD narrowly missing out on an absolute majority of seats in parliament, which would have allowed it to become the first far-right party to govern a German state since World War II.

Siegmund reiterated his intention to implement a radical shift in policy if elected, stating that they have a clear mandate to govern but will not compromise their principles.

The latest projections show Siegmund's AfD on 44% of the vote, narrowly missing out on an absolute majority of seats in parliament, which would have allowed it to become the first far-right party to govern a German state since World War II.

"In a worst-case scenario, there would simply be a new election, and then we'd end up with 50 or 55%," Siegmund told public broadcaster ZDF. "Because the future lies with Alternative for Germany."

The 35-year-old, who would become Germany's youngest ever premier if he is elected, reiterated his intention to implement a radical shift in policy.

"If there is anyone with whom we can achieve this, then we will do so. We have a clear mandate to govern," said Siegmund. "But we will not compromise our principles, and we will not betray ourselves here."

articles.title: Uttarakhand waqf board bid to align nikahnama with UCC draws opposition
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Uttarakhand waqf board's plan to introduce a revised marriage contract, or nikahnama, within a month \"to align it with the Uniform Civil Co.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Uttarakhand waqf board's plan to introduce a revised marriage contract, or nikahnama, within a month "to align it with the Uniform Civil Code" has not gone down well with All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB), which has challenged UCC in the high court.AIMPLB spokesperson SQR Ilyas said that the board opposes any such move by state waqf board and state govt and wants to reiterate that the nikahnama should not be revised till Uttarakhand HC gives its judgement. "Our view is clear that Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act exists and is a valid Indian law. So, how can UCC be used to overrule provisions of an existing personal law on marriage, divorce or inheritance rights? Even today, those who do not want to go by a personal law have the right to recourse under civil laws applicable to all persons. So why a UCC?" Ilyas asked.He said the board is going to challenge UCC passed in Gujarat, Assam and MP, as it has done in Uttarakhand. It will also be taking up the issue of UCC when it launches the "Movement for Protection of the Constitution and Sharia" - a national campaign that will get underway from Jantar Mantar on Sept 17.As reported by TOI, Uttarakhand waqf board authorities are scheduled to meet UCC panel members on Sept 9 to review and refine the draft. The revised document will remove columns for second, third and fourth marriages. Reaffirming that instant talaq is unconstitutional, the contract strictly stipulates single marriages, while the practice of 'halala' will be banned across the state.Conversion solely for marriage will no longer be permitted, requiring individuals wishing to convert to follow procedures outlined under Special Marriage Act of 1954. The mandatory waiting period known as 'iddat' will no longer be enforced, giving women the autonomy to determine the duration themselves.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Maryam Moshiri: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer
articles.summary: Maryam Moshiri tells the BBC she wanted to reveal her diagnosis to raise awareness about the cancer.
articles.body:
BBC News presenter Maryam Moshiri has revealed she is living with blood cancer.

Moshiri, who is one of the corporation's best-known news anchors, told the BBC she wanted to share her diagnosis to raise awareness about the disease.

"It's been two years since my diagnosis and I've felt that I've started to understand the disease a lot better and the way it affects my life. I've got a handle on it to a degree now, so I felt it was really important to raise awareness," the 49-year-old said

"I'm going to have to spend the rest of my life being treated for this," she added.

Moshiri was diagnosed in November 2024 with polycythaemia vera (PV) - a rare, treatable blood cancer. Although it cannot be cured, it can be managed effectively.

In PV, your body makes too many red blood cells, which makes the blood thicker than normal.

It leads to a higher risk of developing blood clots, which can cause a stroke, heart attack or deep vain thrombosis (DVT).

Symptoms can include headaches, confusion, dizziness and blurred vision.

"I was told by my consultant that I have this incurable blood cancer," she said.

"Mostly I had no symptoms and that's one of the problems with this disease.

"The only reason mine was caught was because my GP was so fastidious in the way she did my routine blood tests and immediately sent them for further diagnosis."

As part of her initial treatment, the BBC News chief presenter underwent several "debilitating" hour-long sessions of venesections.

Venesection is a procedure where a needle is put into a vein in the arm to slowly draw the blood out.

This blood letting can be an effective way to reduce the thickness of the blood.

"In about a space of five months, I had venesection seven or eight times. So you can imagine my iron levels hit the floor and I felt even more exhausted," she said.

"After a while I started feeling extremely unwell and tired. I started losing my hair, I got itchy all over my body, but the main symptom was fatigue."

Later, Moshiri was able to get on an immunotherapy treatment called interferon through the NHS, and after some tweaks, she says she is in a better place.

"I've only needed one venosection in about 15 months, so that's been really good. The last couple of months have been better than the last two years," she said.

"I think it's really important people understand that this blood cancer is incurable but it's manageable with the right treatment and you can lead a relatively healthy life.

"It's just a question of finding the right treatment and making sure it works for you."

She admits she is "not the person I was two years ago" but says she feels "much better".

In a few cases, PV can develop into another type of blood cancer called myelofibrosis, and even more rarely can develop into a type of leukaemia called acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), according to charity Blood Cancer UK which funds research into blood cancers.

The mother-of-three said she has had to adjust to life with her condition, sometimes not being able to attend family occasions or play with her children because she is exhausted.

"It's the kind of fatigue that is not like I'm just tired and I didn't get a good night's sleep, you feel like someone has removed your battery completely, and however much sleep you get makes no difference," she explains.

"Even though I feel the best I have in two years, I don't know how I'm going to be in six months, one year, two years.

"People with PV have a higher chance of stroke, heart attack or FVT, so it's something I always have be aware of and make sure I mitigate."

Despite the fatigue, Moshiri has continued to travel across the world covering the biggest stories over the last two years for the BBC, anchoring from Qatar at the start of the US-Israel war with Iran, covering the selection of the new Pope from the Vatican and travelling to Greenland for Vice-President JD Vance's visit.

She credits her "supportive and helpful" husband Jonathan, management at the BBC and her children Iris, 13, Vivienne, 11 and Caspian, 9.

"It took me a long time to be able to tell them about this illness, because I don't want to worry them, but they have been so understanding. When I say things like 'mummy is to tired to play with you', they get it and they don't push it," she said.

Helen Rowntree, chief executive of Blood Cancer UK, said: "We're so grateful to Maryam for bravely sharing her story. When public figures speak openly about their diagnosis, it cuts through the silence that so often surrounds blood cancer – the UK's fifth most common cancer and third biggest cancer killer."

Rowntree said the blood cancer can feel like a "silent" cancer as patients can present with vague, hard to spot symptoms, and highlighted that many with the disease manage their illness, treatment and side-effects alongside work and family life.

"We urgently need continued public and government support to fund the next generation of kinder, more effective treatments with fewer side-effects – so that more people with blood cancer can live well, spend less time dealing with the impact of treatment and be there for the moments that matter," she added.

"There is a lot of research going into blood cancer and scientific advancement to look forward to. Hopefully they'll be some sort of advancement that will help even more than these medications I've been given," Moshiri added.
